fields.why: Main claims rest on monthly proportions, but the text also claims weighted annual visit counts were 8% higher in 2020 (counts per period with no denominator = count/rate).

A's 'summary' quote is itself a 2020 vs 2019 comparison; B's stratified/adjusted rests on a logistic model of whether the year change differs by age and sex, which the brief's rule that period changes within group levels are a 'comparison' series does not clearly cover. Rule needed: say whether a modeled interaction test of a period change across groups lifts depth to stratified/adjusted.

Year changes are compared across three age groups (<18, 18-49/>=18, >=50), so a 3+ group comparison coexists with the 2020 vs 2019 pair; the brief says use group. Both readers record a groupwise age entry, which contradicts B's 'pair'.
No covariate adjustment is described (age and sex are effect modifiers, not confounders), so false fits; null is defensible because the model's specification and results are not reported.

brief_issues: Period-change-within-groups rule vs a modeled interaction across those groups: analytic_depth undecided.
